metadata.title: HDDLGym: A Tool for Studying Multi-Agent Hierarchical Problems Defined in HDDL with OpenAI Gym
metadata.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS 2025, vol. 35)
metadata.abstract_summary: Extends HDDL with agent types so hierarchical multi-agent planning problems can run as Gym environments, with metrics for plan difficulty and for training and deployment.

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text:
What the paper proposes or defines, as extracted (section, page):
- **Agent-centric HDDL domain extension** (category B) - Extends HDDL domains with an agent type hierarchy, agent-parameterized actions, a none action, and explicit task effects so Gym environments can represent multi-agent hierarchical planning. (section 4 Formal Framework, p. 3)
  > An agent-centric planning domain D is a tuple D = ⟨ta, L, TP , TC, M⟩, where:
- **Agent tuple with belief and hierarchy** (category B) - Defines each agent as name, policy, beliefs about other agents' configurations, an action hierarchy of tasks, methods and actions, and an update function. (section 5.2 Agent, p. 4)
  > An agent A is defined with a tuple ⟨N, P, B, H, U⟩where:
- **Hierarchy completion pruning** (category C) - Memory management that removes completed tasks and actions from an agent's hierarchy and its beliefs after each environment step. (section 5.2 Agent, p. 5)
  > comparing their effects with the current state of the world.
- **HDDLGym joint-operator planner** (category D) - Centralized planner building each agent's action hierarchy down to a grounded primitive action; decentralized agents run it using beliefs about other agents. (section 5.5 Planning for Multi-agent Scenarios, p. 6)
  > In case of decentralized planning, the list A include a real agent and that agent’s belief about other agents.
- **Pre-training plan difficulty metrics** (category A) - Estimates domain scalability before training using representation dimensionality, planning time, average planning steps, and random-exploration success rate. (section 6.3 Evaluation Metrics, p. 8)
  > Plan Difficulty of Transport, Overcooked, Rover, and Satellite Problems.
- **Training and deployment evaluation metrics** (category A) - Tracks RL convergence and deployed planner performance with loss, cumulative discounted reward, success rate, planning time, planning steps, plus hierarchy visualization. (section 6.3 Evaluation Metrics, p. 8)
  > Loss plo

sections.heading: Method
sections.text:
- **Agent-centric HDDL domain extension**: Domain D = ⟨ta, L, TP , TC, M⟩ adds ta; agent actions take agent parameters, environment actions auto-execute when preconditions hold; tasks declare :effect checked against world state.
- **Agent tuple with belief and hierarchy**: An agent A is defined with a tuple ⟨N, P, B, H, U⟩: N name, P policy, B beliefs about other agents, H action hierarchy, U hierarchy updater.
- **Hierarchy completion pruning**: U compares task and action effects with current world state; completed items are removed from H and B; U runs after each step function execution.
- **HDDLGym joint-operator planner**: Enumerates valid operators per agent, forms joint combinations C, prunes conflicts, selects c ←argmaxc∈CPO or samples weighted by PO, then updates hierarchies iteratively.
- **Pre-training plan difficulty metrics**: Plan complexity from Table 1 dimensionality counts; difficulty from plan time, number of planning steps, and success rate using random exploration.
- **Training and deployment evaluation metrics**: Loss plots saved at intervals; policy periodically evaluated on cumulative discounted reward, success rate, planning time, planning steps; deployment adds execution time and step-by-step hierarchy visualization.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Evidence the authors report:
  - Agent-centric HDDL domain extension: Applied to IPC-HTN Transport and custom Overcooked domains; Table 2 lists agent-centric domains shipped in the codebase.
  - Agent tuple with belief and hierarchy: Overcooked Figure 1b shows one chef's hierarchy alongside its belief about the other chef's hierarchy.
  - Hierarchy completion pruning: Transport Figure 1a shows the hierarchy shrinking across four steps to a terminal primitive action.
  - HDDLGym joint-operator planner: Algorithm 1; Transport collaboration adds transfer task, method and action, cutting heterogeneous plan length from 25 to 18 steps.
  - Pre-training plan difficulty metrics: Table 3 covers Transport, Overcooked, Rover, Satellite across agent counts; several domains reach 0% success with three or more agents.
  - Training and deployment evaluation metrics: Figure 4 shows PPO actor and critic losses for Transport with 1–3 agents and reward, success rate, planning time, steps for 1-agent Transport.
- Limitations the authors state:
  - Agent-centric HDDL domain extension: Only changes HDDL domain files; not every IPC-HTN domain supports explicit agent specification.
  - HDDLGym joint-operator planner: Assumes a deterministic transition function; action effects are predictable and do not account for probabilistic outcomes.
  - Pre-training plan difficulty metrics: Low success probabilities from exploration increase the risk of low-quality data, which can degrade model performance.
- Limitations they do not state: not assessed. Results are the authors' own, from their simulations, benchmarks or surveys; none evaluates delegation to cheaper models on software work.
